views.title: Registered plan (PLAN_ex3_20261017.md, committed before launch)
views.html:
# PLAN — ex3: does RAE's dimension-dependent noise shift, alone or with the wide head, raise RoboTwin closed-loop success?

Registered 2026-10-17 before launch on shenlong-gpu-01 (authorization: all eight GPUs until 2026-10-18 12:00 America/Chicago).
Written to satisfy `research_lab/TOP_PRIORITY/EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL.md` §2. Study runtime: `/home/zifanz4/openwam-runtime/rae-factorial-20261010`
(mirrored from gpu-02; the 2026-10-10 preregistration in `EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md` is the parent of this file; amendments are listed at the end).

## Question and research question it serves

Research question (user's words, 2026-10-02): can the RAE representation-autoencoder ideas raise the OpenWAM policy's RoboTwin closed-loop success?

This experiment answers, yes / no / by how much, for the 768-dim DINOv3 ("raw768") route:

- **H1** Does changing the training video-noise shift from 5 to 16.4317 (RAE prescription for m = 1,105,920 nominal dims), with the native head, change paired fresh-scene success?
- **H2** Does the RAE wide head (3072 / 24 heads / depth 1 / MLP 2), at shift 5, change paired fresh-scene success? (Replication on fresh scenes of the ex2 reading 24/60 vs 32/60 on adjust_bottle.)
- **H3** Is there an interaction: wide head at shift 16.4317 vs native head at shift 16.4317 (H3a), and shift 16.4317 vs 5 under the wide head (H3b)?

What it cannot answer: whether these changes help a Wan-VAE latent policy (no VAE arm), whether they help at official scale (20k steps, 765 demos, 12-layer 1024-dim DiT only), and anything about the two tasks that were at zero for every arm in ex2 if they stay at zero here (then only adjust_bottle carries information).

## Baseline

`raw768_native` from study `rae-policy-expanded-20261006` (ex2): 20,000 steps on 765 train / 76 dev demos, seeds 42/43/44, source commit `openwam-rae-research@e983676b`.
Trusted evaluation: 60 old scenes × 3 seeds, adjust_bottle 32/60, handover_block 0/60, place_object_basket 0/57; results in
`research/greene/records/rae-factorial-preparation-20261010/originals/evaluation-ledger.json`. Its three checkpoints are reused here unchanged (sha256 in each run's `result.json`); they are re-evaluated on the fresh scenes so every number on one table comes from one protocol (REPORTING rule 19).

## Hypotheses and competing explanations

- H1 (shift): RAE's shift mechanism says high-dimensional latents need more noise during training; the prescription for our latent is 16.43. Competing explanation: the effective dimension of DINOv3 features is far below nominal, so 5 is already adequate and 16.43 only wastes training on near-pure-noise samples. The corrected sigma-curve audit of 2026-10-10 (unweighted MSE ratio 0.997–1.022 across σ) already suggests the two settings fit equally; closed-loop success decides.
- H2 (wide head): a 3072-wide shallow head relieves the 1024-dim trunk bottleneck for 3072-dim patches. Competing explanation: the head fits the video target (dev video loss 3.6× lower in ex1) without changing the action stream, so success is unchanged or lower (ex2: lower).
- H3 (interaction): the RAE paper combines both; either may need the other. The 2×2 design separates them: H3a/H3b are single-variable contrasts at the other factor's new level.

## Intervention (single change per contrast; L0 verified 2026-10-17)

`diff templates/raw768_native/config.yaml templates/raw768_native_shift16/config.yaml` → only `shift_video: 5.0 → 16.4317` (plus output paths).
`diff templates/raw768_wide/config.yaml templates/raw768_wide_shift16/config.yaml` → the same single line.
`diff templates/raw768_native/config.yaml templates/raw768_wide/config.yaml` → only the four `rae_head_*` lines.
Action shift stays 5. Loss, weights, normalization, horizon, deployment steps unchanged.

## Held fixed

Data: `cache.pt` sha256 `2f8419ff…` (6120 train / 304 dev windows), normalization stats `c3012523…`; common initialization per seed (`initialization/common-seed{42,43,44}.safetensors`, hashes in `input-freeze.json`); batch schedule and noise streams paired by seed; 20,000 steps, batch 3 × accumulation 2, AdamW 3e-5, cosine with 1000 warmup; final checkpoint only (no selection by dev loss). Evaluation: the first 20 expert-feasible scenes among 40 fixed candidates per task (seeds 6200000+, 6201000+, 6202000+; overlap with every known protocol checked in `seed-exclusion.json`), clean condition, native success rule, 600 s per episode, frozen policy server (10 denoise steps, horizon 8), one host and one renderer for all 900 attempts. Training uses precomputed latents, so the host change does not touch the training inputs.

## Metrics

Primary: task-balanced paired success-rate difference (candidate − baseline) over 3 tasks × 20 scenes × 3 training seeds, scene-cluster bootstrap 95 % interval (10,000 draws, seed 20261010), per-seed differences reported (`score.py`). Technical failures count as unsuccessful and are reported separately. Secondary: per-task counts, the two-variable diagonal (wide+shift16 vs native, labelled confounded), S-VAE vs raw768. Diagnostic only, never a success claim: fixed-sigma unweighted video MSE and action flow loss (`eval_sigma_curve_v2.py`).

## Predictions

| contrast | predicted direction | rough size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H1 shift16 vs 5 (native head) | no detectable change | \|Δ\| < 5 pp |
| H2 wide vs native (shift 5) | zero or negative, as in ex2 | −5 … 0 pp |
| H3a wide vs native at shift16 | undecided; the paper's claim predicts positive | unknown |
| H3b shift16 vs 5 under wide head | undecided | unknown |

## Criterion (fixed before any result)

Supported: Δ ≥ +5 pp and the interval's lower bound > 0. Refuted: Δ ≤ −5 pp and upper bound < 0. Otherwise undecided; no extra scenes are added to reach significance. Three training seeds do not establish generalization over training randomness; the report says so.

## Budget, deadline, stop and rollback

Estimated: 6 trainings × ~1.5 GPU-h (ex2 measured), 3 scene screenings ≤ 2 h each, 15 evaluation cells × ~2.4 GPU-h ≈ 45 GPU-h; on eight free gpu-01 cards ≈ 8–10 h wall. Hard deadline 2026-10-18 17:00 UTC written into `protocol.json`; every child process is killed at it. Stop and report (no silent fix) when: a preflight fails; a training run fails (no automatic retry, per protocol); a scene screening hits an infrastructure error; the baseline checkpoint fails strict reload or its sha256; the simulator gate (`simulation_smoke.py`) fails on this host; the deadline would be exceeded. Rollback: nothing is merged; the study directory is retained whole.

## Stages (EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL §4)

| stage | here | pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L0 static | config diffs above | done 2026-10-17 |
| L1 one batch | `train.py --preflight` 3 steps per new arm: finite losses, non-zero trunk/action/wide-head gradients, exact serialization | required on gpu-01 before any training (gpu-02's 10-11 pass is archived, not reused) |
| L2 tiny | not applicable to a fixed-recipe retrain; covered by L1 plus `initial-dev.json` | — |
| L3 subset | simulator gate on one training scene per task before each evaluation cell; manual renderer check on this host before the post-workers start | required |
| L4 full | 6 trainings, 3 screenings, 15 cells | the comparison |

## Expected outputs

`runs/<arm>-seed<s>/{result.json, metrics.jsonl, final-dev.json, checkpoint_step_20000.safetensors}`; `scenes/<task>/manifest.json`; `evaluation/fresh/<arm>-seed<s>/<task>/clean/seed-<n>/{result.json, trace.jsonl, frames/}`; `success-summary.json`; a generated logic-tree page with per-contrast tables, policy-input videos (success / median / failure per arm and task) and download buttons.

## Names (EXPERIMENT_NAMING)

| raw768_wide_shift16 ×3 seeds | `ex3-b_wideshift16_1017` | wide head, shift_video 16.4317 | H3 |
| reused ex2 arms | `ex2-a_raw768native_1006`, `ex2-b_widehead_1006`, `ex2-c_svae48_1006` | from `rae-policy-expanded-20261006` | baseline, H2, S |

History table (old name → standard name): `rae-policy-20261001` → ex1 (3 arms, 4000 steps, 66 demos); `rae-policy-expanded-20261006` → ex2; `rae-shift-20261003` → ex0-shift (retracted reading, see `RAE_SHIFT_RESULT.md`).

## Amendments to the 2026-10-10 preregistration (all before launch, none after a result)

1. Host moved from gpu-02 (GPU1/2 idle-only) to gpu-01 (all eight GPUs, shared low-utilization cards allowed); deadline 2026-10-18 17:00 UTC; polling 3 × 60 s; training attempt limit 4 h. (`amend_gpu01_20261017.py`, `resource-amendment-gpu01.json`.)
2. Primary comparison re-registered from the two-variable diagonal to the four single-variable contrasts H1/H2/H3a/H3b (rule 12); the diagonal stays as a labelled confounded secondary. (`score.py`.)
3. Evaluation logs every policy-input frame (JPEG per policy call, three cameras) for the report's videos; success rule and control flow unchanged. (`evaluate_policy.py` patch inside the amendment script.)
4. gpu-02's two preflight passes are archived; preflight is rerun on gpu-01 as the L1 gate for this host.

views.title: H1 — ex3-a: video shift 5 → 16.4317 with the native head
views.html:
Background

RAE (Zheng et al. 2025) prescribes a dimension-dependent noise shift α = √(m/4096); for our 1,105,920-dim raw768 latent that is 16.43, while OpenWAM uses 5. The corrected 2026-10-10 audit found no fit difference (unweighted MSE ratio 0.997–1.022), so success is the only remaining test.

Question

Does training raw768_native with shift_video 16.4317 instead of 5 change paired fresh-scene success?

Single variable, everything else locked

shift_video: 5.0 → 16.4317 in the training config; action shift stays 5. Same 765/76 demonstrations (cache.pt sha256 2f8419ff…), common per-seed initialization, paired batch schedule and noise streams, 20,000 steps, final checkpoint only; same 60 fresh scenes, native success rule, 600 s per episode, one host and renderer for every arm.

Criterion (written before the run)

Supported if Δ ≥ +5 pp and the 95 % interval excludes 0; refuted if Δ ≤ −5 pp and the interval excludes 0; otherwise undecided. Prediction: no detectable change (|Δ| < 5 pp).

What each outcome changes

Supported → the shift prescription transfers to actions and becomes the default for the raw768 route. Refuted → 5 stays and the mechanism is marked as not transferring. Undecided → the raw768 route is not pursued further through the shift; the next decision is the missing Wan-VAE control.

views.title: H3 — ex3-b: wide head and shift 16.4317 together (two single-variable contrasts)
views.html:
Background

The RAE paper uses the wide head together with the shift; either might need the other. ex3-b is the fourth cell of the 2×2 design.

Question

H3a: at shift 16.4317, does the wide head change success (vs raw768_native_shift16)? H3b: under the wide head, does shift 16.4317 change success (vs raw768_wide)?

Single variable, everything else locked

H3a changes only the head; H3b changes only the shift. Same 765/76 demonstrations (cache.pt sha256 2f8419ff…), common per-seed initialization, paired batch schedule and noise streams, 20,000 steps, final checkpoint only; same 60 fresh scenes, native success rule, 600 s per episode, one host and renderer for every arm.

Criterion (written before the run)

Same ±5 pp / interval criterion for each contrast. The two-variable diagonal (wide+shift16 vs native) is reported but labelled confounded. Prediction: undecided.

What each outcome changes

If H3a or H3b is supported while H1 and H2 are not, the effect is an interaction and needs a replication cohort before being used. If none is supported, the RAE transfer to this policy is closed at this scale.

views.title: Fresh-scene evaluation baseline (frozen before any policy is scored)
views.html:
20 expert-feasible scenes per task, taken in order from 40 fixed candidate seeds (6200000+, 6201000+, 6202000+). The expert planner, not any learned policy, decides feasibility; infeasible candidates are retained in the manifest. Overlap with every known training/evaluation seed list was checked (seed-exclusion.json).

taskacceptedattempted candidatesstate
adjust_bottle200complete
handover_block200complete
place_object_basket200complete

Success rule

RoboTwin's native per-task success check at any step within the native step limit (400 / 800 / 700 actions); an episode is a technical failure if the initial render deviates more than 1 uint8 level from the frozen reference, if the 600 s wall limit is hit, or if the simulator errors; technical failures count as unsuccessful in every contrast and are reported separately.

Known gaps

  • handover_block and place_object_basket were at zero for every arm in ex2; if they stay at zero here they carry no information and the contrasts rest on adjust_bottle alone.
  • Rendering on this host uses OIDN 2.3.3 (the only denoiser that runs on Blackwell); the policies were trained on data collected with the same denoiser on gpu-02.
  • Three training seeds; generalization over training randomness is not established.

views.title: Renderer divergence: OIDN 2.3.3 vs the 2.0.1 reference renders
views.html:
Same physics state, same camera: renders on gpu-02 differ from the reference PNGs by 0.51–1.03 uint8 levels (median 0.57). Torch reproduced the deviation to 3–4 decimals by preloading OIDN 2.3.3 on an L40S, so the cause is the denoiser version, not the GPU or driver. OIDN 2.0.1 cannot run on Blackwell (no sm_120 kernels). Consequence: every arm in ex2/ex3 is evaluated with the same 2.3.3 renderer it was trained with; the official checkpoint still reached 58/60 under it.

views.title: Missing control: Wan-VAE 48-dim latent arm (not started)
views.html: RAE's claim is 'representation autoencoder instead of VAE'. Every arm so far is DINOv3-based; the VAE-latent arm with the same backbone, steps, data and seeds has not been run. Proposed on 2026-10-02 (stage 2) and 2026-10-07 (official-standard recipe); waiting for the user's decision. Estimated 3 trainings × ~1 h plus 3 evaluation cells.
